blocks.text: What an AI assistant does inside Apple Mail on Mac

Apple Mail sends, receives, sorts and searches well enough for most days. It does not explain itself. When a send fails or a setting hides in a pane, you search Apple's help or you guess. An AI assistant for Apple Mail on Mac fills that gap. You ask in plain words, and it answers about what is on your screen.

Lazur works from the outside. It is not a plugin or add-in for Mail or any other app. When you hold the shortcut, it looks at your screen and listens. It answers out loud, then points, explains, or types text where your cursor sits.
Apple Mail on Mac problems: not sending, passwords and search

The problems people search for cluster around four areas: sending, logging in, speed and search. Apple's own Mail help page lists 'Can't send email' first. Apple does not say which topics get the most visits, so that order is not a popularity ranking. Third-party guides fill in the rest, and they are anecdotal.

items: Mail will not send. Typical causes are the outgoing (SMTP) server, its port, or a connection that a network blocks.
Mail keeps asking for your password. Keychain is often part of this, so an old saved password can be the cause.
Mail crashes or feels slow, especially with a large mailbox.
Search does not find a message you know arrived. Mailbird points to the Spotlight index as a common cause.
One email account fails while others work. That often points to that account's settings, not to Mail as a whole.

blocks.text: Treat that list as a checklist of likely causes. It comes from a competitor's troubleshooting article and cites no survey. It cannot tell you how many people hit each problem.

blocks.title: Copy the error text
blocks.text: Read out the exact wording of an error, or the name of the account, when you ask. Precise wording gets you to the right fix faster than a general question.
Ask what is on screen and hear the answer
Hold ⌥ ⌘, which means Option and Command together, and ask. Lazur sees the screen at that moment and answers out loud. You do not need to copy text or take a screenshot first.
Questions with one clear answer work best. 'What does this error mean?' is a good one. 'Fix my mail' is too vague to answer well. Lazur can only explain what is on screen and what you tell it.

Here is a worked example. A 'Sending failed' alert is open. You hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask what it means. A useful answer names the likely cause, such as the outgoing server, and says where to check it. From there, open Mail > Settings > Accounts, pick the account, and ask Lazur to explain each field as you reach it.
Point at a button, menu item or setting

Some questions are about location. 'Where is Archive?' and 'Where do I turn on the sidebar?' are typical. Ask out loud and Lazur draws a circle and a label around the item on your screen. You still press the button. Lazur only shows you where it is.

Pointing is slower than a shortcut once you know one. Use pointing for the commands you use once in a while. Learn the shortcuts for the commands you use every day. The table further down lists the ones Apple publishes.
Walk through a Mail feature one click at a time
For a longer task, ask Lazur to walk you through it. It gives one step, then waits for your click before the next. This suits setup work, where one wrong pane can send you back to the start.

Say you want a rule that moves newsletters into a folder. Ask 'Walk me through making a rule in Mail.' Lazur starts with the Mail settings, then the Rules pane. It names each button as it appears, so you always know what to press.
Walk-throughs are slower than a how-to article for someone who knows the app. Use them when you are stuck in one place. For a routine task, a shortcut is faster.
Two habits help. Do not skip the wait, because each step assumes the last one worked. If the screen looks different from what Lazur describes, say so out loud. Then ask again from where you are.
Dictate email on Mac and draft replies

There are two ways to get words into a reply. The first is dictation. Hold fn, speak, and let go. Lazur turns your speech into clean, formatted text at the cursor, in any app. Dictation is included with Lazur.
The second is drafting. Ask Lazur for a reply and it types the draft where your cursor sits. Read every line before you send. Lazur does not press Send for you.

A worked example helps. A colleague asks for a file by Friday. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask for a reply that says the file arrives Friday morning. Read the draft. Then hold fn and dictate the one sentence you want in your own words.

items: Snippets hold text you type all the time, such as a sign-off or an address.
The personal dictionary holds names and product terms that dictation gets wrong.
Clipboard slots keep a few items ready to paste into a reply.

blocks.text: Drafts depend on context. Lazur reads what is on screen. If a long thread is scrolled to the bottom, only the last reply is visible. Scroll to the part you mean before you ask.
Apple Mail keyboard shortcuts on Mac

Apple publishes the reference list for Mail on Mac. Shortcuts change with language and keyboard layout, so the menus are the final check. The table shows the shortcuts Apple lists for the most common tasks.

blocks.text: Shortcuts vary by language and keyboard layout. If a shortcut does nothing, open the menu bar and read the shortcut shown beside that command.
Apple Intelligence in Mail on Mac: requirements

Some Mail features depend on Apple Intelligence. Apple's 'What's new in Mail on Mac' page lists Suggestions, Personalized Writing, and Expanded Search Results. The page does not tie them to a macOS version or give their requirements.

Apple's requirements page says Apple Intelligence in macOS 27 needs a Mac with M1 or later. Your device and Siri language must match a supported language. Storage is the other limit. Macs with M3 or later and at least 12 GB of unified memory need up to 14 GB. Other Apple Intelligence Macs need up to 8 GB.

blocks.title: Check before you upgrade
blocks.text: Apple's macOS 27 product page did not load when this page was checked, so the Mac list is not confirmed here. Read Apple's Apple Intelligence requirements page before you plan an upgrade.
Lazur runs on macOS, on both Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available. You can get the app from the [download page](/download).
How many people use Apple Mail on Mac?

The best recent figure is a secondary summary of Litmus data. It puts Apple Mail at 62.26% of email opens in July 2026. That count covers iPhone, iPad and Mac together, so it does not give a Mac-only share.
The number also leans high. Mailchimp says Apple Mail Privacy Protection reports emails as opened regardless of recipient activity. Some of those opens never came from a person reading the message.
Apple publishes no Mac Mail user count. If you need a number for a report, call it an estimate and name the source.
Privacy: what leaves your Mac when you ask

Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers so they can answer. They are not stored, and content is never used to train AI models.
Lazur also keeps a memory of what you asked and did. That memory stays on the Mac. Close any message you do not want shared before you hold the shortcut.
Mistakes people make with an AI assistant in Mail

items: Asking before the message is open. Open it first, then hold ⌥ ⌘.
Holding fn to ask a question. fn is for dictation. Use ⌥ ⌘ to ask about the screen.
Expecting Lazur to send, archive or delete. It points and types. You click.
Sending a draft unread. Check names, dates and tone first.
Skipping the wait in a walk-through. Each step depends on the one before.

blocks.text: Edge cases: language, versions and multiple accounts

Language is the first edge case. Shortcut names and menu labels follow the language you use. Apple Intelligence also needs your device and Siri language to match a supported language. If one is off, ask in the language your menus use.

Version is the second. Apple's Mail User Guide for Mac is labelled for macOS 27 and has a selector that goes back to macOS High Sierra. The Mail app's version number is not confirmed in Apple's text, so follow what your screen shows.
Multiple accounts are the third. A failure in one account is often that account's settings. Ask Lazur which account the error names, then check that account first.
Try it on one real message

items: Open one message that shows an error, or one that needs a reply.
Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask what the message or error means. Listen to the answer.
Ask where the next button is. Lazur circles it. You press it.
Hold fn and dictate a short reply. Then ask for a shorter draft and compare.
Read the final text, then send it yourself.

faq.question: Does Lazur plug into Apple Mail?
faq.answer: No. Lazur is not a plugin or add-in for Mail or any other app. It is a voice assistant for the Mac that works across apps, including Mail. It answers and points, but it does not operate Mail for you.

faq.question: Can Lazur send, archive or delete my email?
faq.answer: No. Lazur points at buttons, explains what is on screen, walks you through steps, and types drafts or dictated text. It does not click buttons or operate other apps for you. You press Send, Archive or Delete yourself.

faq.question: Which key do I hold in Mail?
faq.answer: Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about anything on screen, and Lazur answers out loud. Hold fn to dictate clean text at the cursor. Use fn for speech and ⌥ ⌘ for questions.

faq.question: Does Lazur work with the Apple Intelligence features in Mail?
faq.answer: Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. The Mail features that use Apple Intelligence have their own requirements. Apple lists a Mac with M1 or later for macOS 27, and your device and Siri language must match. Check Apple's requirements page before you rely on those features.

faq.question: Why does Mail keep asking for my password?
faq.answer: Third-party troubleshooting guides link repeated password prompts to Keychain. Open Keychain Access, find the entry for that mail account, and check that it is current. Then re-enter the password in Mail > Settings > Accounts. Ask Lazur to walk you through each step.

faq.question: What happens to my mail content when I use Lazur?
faq.answer: Lazur sees what is on screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Lazur also keeps a memory of your requests on the Mac.

faq.question: Is Apple Mail the most used email app on Mac?
faq.answer: No Mac-only figure exists. The best recent number is a secondary summary that puts Apple Mail at 62.26% of email opens across iPhone, iPad and Mac in July 2026. Treat it as a rough signal, not a count of Mac users.

faq.question: How much does Lazur cost?
faq.answer: Lazur has a Pro trial that needs no credit card, then paid plans. Current prices are on the pricing page, so check there rather than rely on this page. Dictation is included on both plans.

faq.question: Why do the shortcuts in this guide not match my Mail?
faq.answer: Apple's shortcuts vary by language and keyboard layout. The menu bar shows the correct shortcut beside each command, so use that as the final check.
